# Demonstrations
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_sign_law(systems: Sequence[Tuple[str, DualEigensystem]]) -> None:
    banner("1.  THE DUALITY SIGN LAW      prod a_i = (-1)^nu * Q^d")
    print(f"{'system':26s} {'d':>2s} {'nu':>3s} {'m+':>3s} "
          f"{'prod alpha':>22s} {'(-1)^nu Q^d':>22s}")
    print("-" * 78)
    for name, E in systems:
        E.check_axioms(require_involutive=E.is_involutive)
        predicted = (-1) ** E.nu * E.Q ** E.deg
        ok = close(E.prod_alpha, predicted)
        mark = "OK " if ok or not E.is_involutive else "!! "
        if not E.is_involutive:
            mark = "n/a"  # the law needs involutivity
        print(f"{name:26s} {E.deg:2d} {E.nu:3d} {E.central_order:3d} "
              f"{fmt(E.prod_alpha):>22s} {fmt(predicted):>22s}  {mark}")
    print()
    print("  'n/a' marks the non-involutive 3-cycle, where the law legitimately")
    print("  fails: involutivity is exactly what the pairing argument consumes.")


def demo_functional_equation(systems: Sequence[Tuple[str, DualEigensystem]]) -> None:
    banner("2.  THE FUNCTIONAL EQUATION   (Q^2 T)^d P(1/(Q^2 T)) = eps Q^d P(T)")
    test_points = [0.37 + 0.21j, -1.4 + 0.9j, 2.1 - 0.6j]
    print(f"{'system':26s} {'eps (def)':>12s} {'(-1)^(d+nu)':>13s} "
          f"{'(-1)^m+':>9s} {'max FE error':>14s}")
    print("-" * 78)
    for name, E in systems:
        worst = 0.0
        for T in test_points:
            lhs = (E.Q ** 2 * T) ** E.deg * E.char_poly(1 / (E.Q ** 2 * T))
            rhs = E.root_sign * E.Q ** E.deg * E.char_poly(T)
            worst = max(worst, abs(lhs - rhs) / max(1.0, abs(rhs)))
        combi = E.root_sign_from_fixed_points() if E.is_involutive else 0
        combi_s = f"{combi:+d}" if E.is_involutive else "  n/a"
        central = E.root_sign_from_central_order() if E.is_involutive else 0
        central_s = f"{central:+d}" if E.is_involutive else "  n/a"
        print(f"{name:26s} {fmt(E.root_sign):>12s} {combi_s:>13s} "
              f"{central_s:>9s} {worst:14.3e}")
    print()
    print("  The functional equation holds for EVERY system (it needs only that")
    print("  sigma is a bijection).  The three sign columns agree exactly when")
    print("  sigma is an involution -- that is the content of the sign law and")
    print("  of the central parity law.")


def demo_central_parity(systems: Sequence[Tuple[str, DualEigensystem]]) -> None:
    banner("3.  CENTRAL PARITY   eps = (-1)^{m+},   P(T) = (1-QT)^{m+} G(T)")
    print(f"{'system':26s} {'m+':>3s} {'P(1/Q)':>14s} {'G(1/Q)':>16s} "
          f"{'eps':>6s}")
    print("-" * 78)
    for name, E in systems:
        if not E.is_involutive:
            continue
        Pc = E.char_poly(1 / E.Q)
        Gc = E.central_factor(1 / E.Q)
        # verify the factorisation at a random point
        T = 0.83 - 0.41j
        lhs = E.char_poly(T)
        rhs = (1 - E.Q * T) ** E.central_order * E.central_factor(T)
        assert close(lhs, rhs), "central factorisation failed"
        print(f"{name:26s} {E.central_order:3d} {fmt(Pc):>14s} {fmt(Gc):>16s} "
              f"{E.root_sign_from_central_order():+6d}")
    print()
    print("  G(1/Q) is never zero, so m+ is EXACTLY the order of vanishing of P")
    print("  at the central point T = 1/Q.  Whenever eps = -1 the multiplicity m+")
    print("  is odd, hence positive, hence P(1/Q) = 0: sign -1 forces central")
    print("  vanishing.")


def demo_structure(Q: complex) -> None:
    banner("4.  STRUCTURE   eps^2 = 1,  multiplicativity,  twist invariance")
    A = pos_fixed(Q)                       # d = 1, eps = -1
    B = duality_pair(Q, 1.7 - 0.9j)        # d = 2, eps = +1
    C = neg_fixed_one(Q)                   # d = 1, eps = +1
    print("  eps^2 = 1 for every system:")
    for name, E in [("pos_fixed", A), ("duality_pair", B), ("neg_fixed", C)]:
        print(f"    {name:16s} eps = {fmt(E.root_sign)}   "
              f"eps^2 = {fmt(E.root_sign ** 2)}")
    print()
    print("  Multiplicativity under direct sums,  eps(E + F) = eps(E) eps(F):")
    for (n1, E), (n2, F) in [(("A", A), ("B", B)),
                             (("A", A), ("C", C)),
                             (("B", B), ("C", C))]:
        S = direct_sum(E, F)
        S.check_axioms()
        print(f"    eps({n1}+{n2}) = {fmt(S.root_sign)}   "
              f"eps({n1})eps({n2}) = {fmt(E.root_sign * F.root_sign)}   "
              f"deg {S.deg} = {E.deg}+{F.deg}   "
              f"m+ {S.central_order} = {E.central_order}+{F.central_order}")
    print()
    print("  Twist invariance,  (Q, a) -> (cQ, ca):")
    for c in [2.0 + 0j, -1.0 + 0j, 0.3 + 1.1j]:
        Bt = twist(B, c)
        Bt.check_axioms()
        At = twist(A, c)
        At.check_axioms()
        print(f"    c = {fmt(c):>18s}   eps(A^c) = {fmt(At.root_sign)}   "
              f"eps(B^c) = {fmt(Bt.root_sign)}")


def demo_odd_degree(Q: complex) -> None:
    banner("5.  ODD DEGREE FORCES CENTRAL VANISHING")
    # d = 3: one +Q fixed point plus one duality pair; no -Q fixed point.
    E = DualEigensystem(
        Q=Q, alpha=(Q, 2.3 + 1.1j, Q ** 2 / (2.3 + 1.1j)), sigma=(0, 2, 1)
    )
    E.check_axioms()
    print(f"    degree d              = {E.deg}  (odd)")
    print(f"    a -Q fixed point?     = {'yes' if E.nu else 'no'}")
    print(f"    a fixed point exists? = "
          f"{'yes' if any(E.sigma[i] == i for i in range(E.deg)) else 'no'}")
    print(f"    central multiplicity  = {E.central_order}  (odd)")
    print(f"    root sign eps         = {fmt(E.root_sign)}  = (-1)^d")
    print(f"    P(1/Q)                = {fmt(E.char_poly(1 / E.Q))}")
    print()
    print("  An involution of an odd-sized set must have a fixed point; with no")
    print("  -Q fixed point allowed, that fixed point carries +Q, so m+ is odd,")
    print("  eps = -1, and the characteristic polynomial vanishes at the centre.")


def demo_analytic_bridge(systems: Sequence[Tuple[str, DualEigensystem]]) -> None:
    banner("6.  ANALYTIC BRIDGE   Lambda(2-s) = eps Lambda(s),  "
           "(-1)^ord = eps = (-1)^{m+}")
    print(f"{'system':26s} {'max FE error':>14s} {'ord_{s=1}':>10s} "
          f"{'(-1)^ord':>9s} {'eps':>6s}")
    print("-" * 78)
    for name, E in systems:
        if not E.is_involutive:
            continue
        L = cmath.log(E.Q)
        worst = 0.0
        for s in [0.4 + 0.3j, 1.9 - 0.7j, 2.6 + 1.2j, 1.0 + 0j]:
            lhs = E.completed_L(2 - s, L)
            rhs = E.root_sign * E.completed_L(s, L)
            worst = max(worst, abs(lhs - rhs) / max(1.0, abs(rhs)))
        r = numerical_order_of_vanishing(lambda s: E.completed_L(s, L), 1.0 + 0j)
        print(f"{name:26s} {worst:14.3e} {r:10d} {(-1) ** r:+9d} "
              f"{E.root_sign_from_central_order():+6d}")
    print()
    print("  The order of vanishing is measured numerically, by Cauchy integrals")
    print("  for the Taylor coefficients of the entire function Lambda around")
    print("  s = 1.  Its parity always reproduces the combinatorial sign, and in")
    print("  every case here it equals m+ on the nose.")


def demo_sharpness(Q: complex) -> None:
    banner("7.  SHARPNESS: EVERY HYPOTHESIS IS LOAD-BEARING")

    print("  (a)  A single -Q fixed point flips the sign (degree 1):")
    for name, E in [("alpha = +Q", pos_fixed(Q)), ("alpha = -Q", neg_fixed_one(Q))]:
        print(f"       {name:12s} prod alpha = {fmt(E.prod_alpha):>14s}   "
              f"Q^d = {fmt(Q ** E.deg):>14s}   eps = {fmt(E.root_sign)}   "
              f"(-1)^d = {(-1) ** E.deg:+d}")
    print()

    print("  (b)  Two -Q fixed points cancel: hypothesis FAILS, conclusion HOLDS.")
    E = two_neg_fixed(Q)
    print(f"       nu = {E.nu} (even)   prod alpha = {fmt(E.prod_alpha)}   "
          f"Q^2 = {fmt(Q ** 2)}   eps = {fmt(E.root_sign)}")
    print()

    print("  (c)  Two-cycles are sign-neutral, whatever the eigenvalue:")
    for a in [1.0 + 0j, 5.5 - 3.2j, 0.04 + 0.01j]:
        E = duality_pair(Q, a)
        print(f"       a = {fmt(a):>20s}   prod alpha = {fmt(E.prod_alpha):>14s}"
              f"   eps = {fmt(E.root_sign)}")
    print()

    print("  (d)  Degree 4: the sign is not a function of the degree alone.")
    for name, E in [("two pairs", two_pairs(Q, 1.3 + 0.4j, -2.2 + 0.7j)),
                    ("(+Q, -Q, a, Q^2/a)", mixed_deg4(Q, 1.9 - 0.5j))]:
        print(f"       {name:20s} prod alpha = {fmt(E.prod_alpha):>16s}   "
              f"eps = {fmt(E.root_sign)}   (-1)^d = {(-1) ** E.deg:+d}")
    print()

    print("  (e)  Involutivity cannot be weakened to bijectivity.")
    E = three_cycle(Q)
    E.check_axioms(require_involutive=False)
    print(f"       sigma = 3-cycle; fixed points: "
          f"{[i for i in range(3) if E.sigma[i] == i]} (none!)")
    print(f"       duality holds at every index, but sigma o sigma != id.")
    print(f"       prod alpha = {fmt(E.prod_alpha)}   "
          f"-Q^3 = {fmt(-Q ** 3)}   Q^3 = {fmt(Q ** 3)}")
    print(f"       eps = {fmt(E.root_sign)}, i.e. (-1)^(d+1), not (-1)^d.")
    print()
    print("       Reason: chasing a_i a_{sigma(i)} = Q^2 around a 3-cycle forces")
    print("       a_0 = a_2 and then a_0^2 = Q^2, so the cycle is constant +-Q.")


def demo_random_stress_test(n_trials: int = 400, seed: int = 20260823) -> None:
    banner("8.  RANDOMISED STRESS TEST OF THE THREE SIGN FORMULAS")
    import random

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    failures = 0
    for _ in range(n_trials):
        Q = complex(rng.uniform(0.4, 3.0), rng.uniform(-2.0, 2.0))
        if abs(Q) < 0.3:
            continue
        n_pairs = rng.randint(0, 3)
        n_pos = rng.randint(0, 3)
        n_neg = rng.randint(0, 3)
        alpha: List[complex] = []
        sigma: List[int] = []
        for _ in range(n_pairs):
            a = complex(rng.uniform(-3, 3), rng.uniform(-3, 3))
            if abs(a) < 0.2:
                a = 0.5 + 0.5j
            k = len(alpha)
            alpha += [a, Q ** 2 / a]
            sigma += [k + 1, k]
        for _ in range(n_pos):
            k = len(alpha)
            alpha.append(Q)
            sigma.append(k)
        for _ in range(n_neg):
            k = len(alpha)
            alpha.append(-Q)
            sigma.append(k)
        if not alpha:
            continue
        E = DualEigensystem(Q=Q, alpha=tuple(alpha), sigma=tuple(sigma))
        E.check_axioms()
        eps = E.root_sign
        s1 = E.root_sign_from_fixed_points()
        s2 = E.root_sign_from_central_order()
        T = complex(rng.uniform(0.3, 2.0), rng.uniform(0.3, 2.0))
        lhs = (Q ** 2 * T) ** E.deg * E.char_poly(1 / (Q ** 2 * T))
        rhs = eps * Q ** E.deg * E.char_poly(T)
        ok = (close(eps, s1) and close(eps, s2)
              and abs(lhs - rhs) <= 1e-5 * max(1.0, abs(rhs)))
        if not ok:
            failures += 1
            print(f"    FAILURE: Q={Q}, alpha={alpha}, sigma={sigma}")
    print(f"    {n_trials} random duality eigensystems tested "
          f"(degrees 1-12, random complex Q).")
    print(f"    Formulas checked:  eps (definition)  ==  (-1)^(d+nu)  "
          f"==  (-1)^{{m+}},")
    print(f"    plus the functional equation at a random point.")
    print(f"    Failures: {failures}")


def main() -> None:
    Q: complex = 1.6 + 0.7j  # nothing requires Q real or positive

    systems: List[Tuple[str, DualEigensystem]] = [
        ("d=1, +Q fixed point", pos_fixed(Q)),
        ("d=1, -Q fixed point", neg_fixed_one(Q)),
        ("d=2, duality pair", duality_pair(Q, 1.7 - 0.9j)),
        ("d=2, two -Q fixed", two_neg_fixed(Q)),
        ("d=4, two pairs", two_pairs(Q, 1.3 + 0.4j, -2.2 + 0.7j)),
        ("d=4, (+Q,-Q,a,Q^2/a)", mixed_deg4(Q, 1.9 - 0.5j)),
        ("d=3, 3-cycle (NOT inv.)", three_cycle(Q)),
    ]

    print(__doc__.split("Run:")[0].rstrip())
    print(f"\nHalf-weight used throughout:  Q = {fmt(Q)}")

    demo_sign_law(systems)
    demo_functional_equation(systems)
    demo_central_parity(systems)
    demo_structure(Q)
    demo_odd_degree(Q)
    demo_analytic_bridge(systems)
    demo_sharpness(Q)
    demo_random_stress_test()

    banner("SUMMARY")
    print("""
    prod a_i    = (-1)^nu Q^d                       (duality sign law)
    eps         = (-1)^(d + nu) = (-1)^{m+}          (central parity law)
    P(T)        = (1 - QT)^{m+} G(T),  G(1/Q) != 0   (exact central order)
    eps = -1    ==>  P(1/Q) = 0                      (central vanishing)
    Lambda(2-s) = eps Lambda(s),  (-1)^ord = eps     (analytic bridge)

    All the sign information in a duality-symmetric spectrum is concentrated
    in the two real points +-Q of the Weil circle -- and there, only in a
    parity.
    """)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

demos.name: Complete Numerical Tour of the Duality Sign Law
demos.description: A self-contained walkthrough of every result in the theory, evaluated on explicit complex eigensystems. It builds duality eigensystems from three ingredients (free two-cycles, +Q fixed points and -Q fixed points), then verifies numerically: the sign law that the eigenvalue product is (-1)^nu times Q^d; the polynomial functional equation at several test points; the agreement of the three independent computations of the sign (its definition, the fixed-point formula (-1)^(d+nu), and the intrinsic central-parity formula (-1)^{m+}); the central factorisation P(T) = (1-QT)^{m+} G(T) with G(1/Q) nonzero; multiplicativity under direct sums and invariance under Tate-twist rescaling; the odd-degree forcing of central vanishing; the analytic functional equation Lambda(2-s) = eps Lambda(s) together with a Cauchy-integral measurement of the order of vanishing at s = 1; all sharpness witnesses including the non-involutive three-cycle; and a randomised stress test over 400 eigensystems of degrees 1 to 12 with random complex half-weights.
demos.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
The Functional-Equation Sign of a Duality Eigensystem
=====================================================

Numerical demonstration of the sign law for duality eigensystems.

A *duality eigensystem* is a triple (Q, alpha, sigma) where

    * Q != 0                       (the half-weight, modelling q^{n/2}),
    * alpha = (a_0, ..., a_{d-1})  (the eigenvalues),
    * sigma  a permutation of {0, ..., d-1}

satisfying

    (Involutivity)  sigma(sigma(i)) = i        for all i,
    (Duality)       a_i * a_{sigma(i)} = Q^2   for all i.

The results demonstrated here:

    1.  Duality sign law:      prod a_i = (-1)^nu * Q^d,
        where nu = #{i : sigma(i) = i and a_i = -Q}.

    2.  Functional equation:   (Q^2 T)^d P(1/(Q^2 T)) = eps * Q^d * P(T),
        where P(T) = prod (1 - a_i T)  and  eps = (-1)^(d + nu).

    3.  Central parity law:    eps = (-1)^{m_+},  m_+ = #{i : a_i = Q}.
        The duality permutation has disappeared from the answer.

    4.  Central factorisation: P(T) = (1 - Q T)^{m_+} G(T),  G(1/Q) != 0,
        so m_+ is exactly the order of vanishing of P at the central point.
        Hence eps = -1  implies  P(1/Q) = 0.

    5.  Structure:             eps^2 = 1; eps is multiplicative under direct
        sums; eps is invariant under the rescaling (Q, a) -> (cQ, ca).

    6.  Analytic bridge:       with e^L = Q and Lambda(s) = e^{(s-1)dL/2} P(e^{-sL}),
        one has Lambda(2 - s) = eps * Lambda(s), and the parity of the order of
        vanishing of Lambda at s = 1 equals eps.

    7.  Sharpness:             a single (-Q) fixed point flips the sign; two of
        them cancel; and a *non-involutive* fixed-point-free 3-cycle breaks the
        conclusion outright (prod a_i = -Q^3).

Run:  python3 demo.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import cmath
import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Callable, List, Sequence, Tuple

TOL: float = 1e-8


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DualEigensystem:
    """A duality eigensystem (Q, alpha, sigma) over the complex numbers.

    ``sigma`` is stored as a list with ``sigma[i]`` the image of ``i``.
    """

    Q: complex
    alpha: Tuple[complex, ...]
    sigma: Tuple[int, ...]

    # -- axioms ------------------------------------------------------------

    def check_axioms(self, require_involutive: bool = True) -> None:
        """Raise ValueError unless the duality-eigensystem axioms hold."""
        d = self.deg
        if abs(self.Q) < TOL:
            raise ValueError("Q must be nonzero")
        if sorted(self.sigma) != list(range(d)):
            raise ValueError("sigma must be a permutation")
        for i in range(d):
            if abs(self.alpha[i] * self.alpha[self.sigma[i]] - self.Q ** 2) > TOL:
                raise ValueError(f"duality fails at index {i}")
        if require_involutive:
            for i in range(d):
                if self.sigma[self.sigma[i]] != i:
                    raise ValueError(f"sigma is not an involution at index {i}")

    @property
    def is_involutive(self) -> bool:
        return all(self.sigma[self.sigma[i]] == i for i in range(self.deg))

    # -- basic invariants --------------------------------------------------

    @property
    def deg(self) -> int:
        """The degree d = number of eigenvalues (the Betti number)."""
        return len(self.alpha)

    @property
    def neg_fixed(self) -> List[int]:
        """Indices fixed by duality whose eigenvalue is -Q."""
        return [
            i
            for i in range(self.deg)
            if self.sigma[i] == i and abs(self.alpha[i] + self.Q) < TOL
        ]

    @property
    def nu(self) -> int:
        """nu = number of anti-diagonal (-Q) fixed points."""
        return len(self.neg_fixed)

    @property
    def central_order(self) -> int:
        """m_+ = multiplicity of the central eigenvalue +Q."""
        return sum(1 for a in self.alpha if abs(a - self.Q) < TOL)

    @property
    def prod_alpha(self) -> complex:
        p: complex = 1.0 + 0j
        for a in self.alpha:
            p *= a
        return p

    # -- the sign ----------------------------------------------------------

    @property
    def root_sign(self) -> complex:
        """eps = (-1)^d * prod(alpha) / Q^d  (Definition of the root sign)."""
        return (-1.0) ** self.deg * self.prod_alpha / self.Q ** self.deg

    def root_sign_from_fixed_points(self) -> int:
        """eps computed combinatorially as (-1)^(d + nu)."""
        return (-1) ** ((self.deg + self.nu) % 2)

    def root_sign_from_central_order(self) -> int:
        """eps computed intrinsically as (-1)^{m_+}: no knowledge of sigma."""
        return (-1) ** (self.central_order % 2)

    # -- polynomials -------------------------------------------------------

    def char_poly(self, T: complex) -> complex:
        """P(T) = prod (1 - a_i T)."""
        p: complex = 1.0 + 0j
        for a in self.alpha:
            p *= 1 - a * T
        return p

    def central_factor(self, T: complex) -> complex:
        """G(T) = prod over {a_i != Q} of (1 - a_i T)."""
        p: complex = 1.0 + 0j
        for a in self.alpha:
            if abs(a - self.Q) >= TOL:
                p *= 1 - a * T
        return p

    # -- analytic bridge ---------------------------------------------------

    def completed_L(self, s: complex, L: complex | None = None) -> complex:
        """Lambda(s) = e^{(s-1) d L / 2} * P(e^{-sL}),  with e^L = Q."""
        if L is None:
            L = cmath.log(self.Q)
        return cmath.exp((s - 1) * self.deg / 2 * L) * self.char_poly(cmath.exp(-s * L))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constructors: the standard families and the sharpness witnesses
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def pos_fixed(Q: complex) -> DualEigensystem:
    """Degree 1, the +Q fixed point.  eps = -1 = (-1)^1."""
    return DualEigensystem(Q=Q, alpha=(Q,), sigma=(0,))


def neg_fixed_one(Q: complex) -> DualEigensystem:
    """Degree 1, the -Q fixed point.  eps = +1 != (-1)^1: the sign flip."""
    return DualEigensystem(Q=Q, alpha=(-Q,), sigma=(0,))


def duality_pair(Q: complex, a: complex) -> DualEigensystem:
    """Degree 2, a single free duality 2-cycle {a, Q^2/a}.  Sign-neutral."""
    return DualEigensystem(Q=Q, alpha=(a, Q ** 2 / a), sigma=(1, 0))


def two_neg_fixed(Q: complex) -> DualEigensystem:
    """Degree 2, two -Q fixed points.  Hypothesis fails, conclusion holds."""
    return DualEigensystem(Q=Q, alpha=(-Q, -Q), sigma=(0, 1))


def two_pairs(Q: complex, a: complex, b: complex) -> DualEigensystem:
    """Degree 4, two duality 2-cycles.  eps = +1 = (-1)^4."""
    return DualEigensystem(
        Q=Q, alpha=(a, Q ** 2 / a, b, Q ** 2 / b), sigma=(1, 0, 3, 2)
    )


def mixed_deg4(Q: complex, a: complex) -> DualEigensystem:
    """Degree 4: (+Q, -Q, a, Q^2/a).  eps = -1 != (-1)^4."""
    return DualEigensystem(Q=Q, alpha=(Q, -Q, a, Q ** 2 / a), sigma=(0, 1, 3, 2))


def three_cycle(Q: complex) -> DualEigensystem:
    """NOT an involution: sigma is the 3-cycle, alpha = (-Q, -Q, -Q).

    Duality holds, sigma has no fixed point at all, yet prod alpha = -Q^3.
    """
    return DualEigensystem(Q=Q, alpha=(-Q, -Q, -Q), sigma=(1, 2, 0))


def direct_sum(E: DualEigensystem, F: DualEigensystem) -> DualEigensystem:
    """Concatenate two eigensystems of the same half-weight Q."""
    if abs(E.Q - F.Q) > TOL:
        raise ValueError("direct sums require equal half-weight Q")
    d = E.deg
    return DualEigensystem(
        Q=E.Q,
        alpha=E.alpha + F.alpha,
        sigma=E.sigma + tuple(d + j for j in F.sigma),
    )


def twist(E: DualEigensystem, c: complex) -> DualEigensystem:
    """(Q, alpha) -> (cQ, c*alpha): the model's Tate twist."""
    if abs(c) < TOL:
        raise ValueError("twist scalar must be nonzero")
    return DualEigensystem(
        Q=c * E.Q, alpha=tuple(c * a for a in E.alpha), sigma=E.sigma
    )


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Numerical utilities
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def numerical_order_of_vanishing(
    f: Callable[[complex], complex],
    center: complex,
    max_order: int = 8,
    radius: float = 0.35,
    n_nodes: int = 512,
) -> int:
    """Order of vanishing of an analytic ``f`` at ``center``.

    Computes Taylor coefficients c_k by the Cauchy integral
    c_k = (1/2 pi i) * int f(z) / (z - center)^{k+1} dz, discretised on a
    circle of the given radius via the trapezoidal rule (spectrally accurate
    for analytic integrands), and returns the least k with |c_k| above a
    relative threshold.
    """
    scale = max(
        abs(f(center + radius * cmath.exp(2j * math.pi * t / n_nodes)))
        for t in range(n_nodes)
    )
    threshold = max(scale, 1.0) * 1e-7
    for k in range(max_order + 1):
        acc = 0.0 + 0j
        for t in range(n_nodes):
            theta = 2 * math.pi * t / n_nodes
            z = center + radius * cmath.exp(1j * theta)
            acc += f(z) * cmath.exp(-1j * k * theta)
        c_k = acc / (n_nodes * radius ** k)
        if abs(c_k) > threshold:
            return k
    return max_order + 1


def close(x: complex, y: complex, tol: float = 1e-6) -> bool:
    return abs(x - y) <= tol * max(1.0, abs(x), abs(y))


def fmt(z: complex) -> str:
    if abs(z.imag) < 1e-9:
        return f"{z.real:+.6f}"
    return f"{z.real:+.6f}{z.imag:+.6f}i"


def banner(text: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(text)
    print("=" * 78)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstrations
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_sign_law(systems: Sequence[Tuple[str, DualEigensystem]]) -> None:
    banner("1.  THE DUALITY SIGN LAW      prod a_i = (-1)^nu * Q^d")
    print(f"{'system':26s} {'d':>2s} {'nu':>3s} {'m+':>3s} "
          f"{'prod alpha':>22s} {'(-1)^nu Q^d':>22s}")
    print("-" * 78)
    for name, E in systems:
        E.check_axioms(require_involutive=E.is_involutive)
        predicted = (-1) ** E.nu * E.Q ** E.deg
        ok = close(E.prod_alpha, predicted)
        mark = "OK " if ok or not E.is_involutive else "!! "
        if not E.is_involutive:
            mark = "n/a"  # the law needs involutivity
        print(f"{name:26s} {E.deg:2d} {E.nu:3d} {E.central_order:3d} "
              f"{fmt(E.prod_alpha):>22s} {fmt(predicted):>22s}  {mark}")
    print()
    print("  'n/a' marks the non-involutive 3-cycle, where the law legitimately")
    print("  fails: involutivity is exactly what the pairing argument consumes.")


def demo_functional_equation(systems: Sequence[Tuple[str, DualEigensystem]]) -> None:
    banner("2.  THE FUNCTIONAL EQUATION   (Q^2 T)^d P(1/(Q^2 T)) = eps Q^d P(T)")
    test_points = [0.37 + 0.21j, -1.4 + 0.9j, 2.1 - 0.6j]
    print(f"{'system':26s} {'eps (def)':>12s} {'(-1)^(d+nu)':>13s} "
          f"{'(-1)^m+':>9s} {'max FE error':>14s}")
    print("-" * 78)
    for name, E in systems:
        worst = 0.0
        for T in test_points:
            lhs = (E.Q ** 2 * T) ** E.deg * E.char_poly(1 / (E.Q ** 2 * T))
            rhs = E.root_sign * E.Q ** E.deg * E.char_poly(T)
            worst = max(worst, abs(lhs - rhs) / max(1.0, abs(rhs)))
        combi = E.root_sign_from_fixed_points() if E.is_involutive else 0
        combi_s = f"{combi:+d}" if E.is_involutive else "  n/a"
        central = E.root_sign_from_central_order() if E.is_involutive else 0
        central_s = f"{central:+d}" if E.is_involutive else "  n/a"
        print(f"{name:26s} {fmt(E.root_sign):>12s} {combi_s:>13s} "
              f"{central_s:>9s} {worst:14.3e}")
    print()
    print("  The functional equation holds for EVERY system (it needs only that")
    print("  sigma is a bijection).  The three sign columns agree exactly when")
    print("  sigma is an involution -- that is the content of the sign law and")
    print("  of the central parity law.")


def demo_central_parity(systems: Sequence[Tuple[str, DualEigensystem]]) -> None:
    banner("3.  CENTRAL PARITY   eps = (-1)^{m+},   P(T) = (1-QT)^{m+} G(T)")
    print(f"{'system':26s} {'m+':>3s} {'P(1/Q)':>14s} {'G(1/Q)':>16s} "
          f"{'eps':>6s}")
    print("-" * 78)
    for name, E in systems:
        if not E.is_involutive:
            continue
        Pc = E.char_poly(1 / E.Q)
        Gc = E.central_factor(1 / E.Q)
        # verify the factorisation at a random point
        T = 0.83 - 0.41j
        lhs = E.char_poly(T)
        rhs = (1 - E.Q * T) ** E.central_order * E.central_factor(T)
        assert close(lhs, rhs), "central factorisation failed"
        print(f"{name:26s} {E.central_order:3d} {fmt(Pc):>14s} {fmt(Gc):>16s} "
              f"{E.root_sign_from_central_order():+6d}")
    print()
    print("  G(1/Q) is never zero, so m+ is EXACTLY the order of vanishing of P")
    print("  at the central point T = 1/Q.  Whenever eps = -1 the multiplicity m+")
    print("  is odd, hence positive, hence P(1/Q) = 0: sign -1 forces central")
    print("  vanishing.")


def demo_structure(Q: complex) -> None:
    banner("4.  STRUCTURE   eps^2 = 1,  multiplicativity,  twist invariance")
    A = pos_fixed(Q)                       # d = 1, eps = -1
    B = duality_pair(Q, 1.7 - 0.9j)        # d = 2, eps = +1
    C = neg_fixed_one(Q)                   # d = 1, eps = +1
    print("  eps^2 = 1 for every system:")
    for name, E in [("pos_fixed", A), ("duality_pair", B), ("neg_fixed", C)]:
        print(f"    {name:16s} eps = {fmt(E.root_sign)}   "
              f"eps^2 = {fmt(E.root_sign ** 2)}")
    print()
    print("  Multiplicativity under direct sums,  eps(E + F) = eps(E) eps(F):")
    for (n1, E), (n2, F) in [(("A", A), ("B", B)),
                             (("A", A), ("C", C)),
                             (("B", B), ("C", C))]:
        S = direct_sum(E, F)
        S.check_axioms()
        print(f"    eps({n1}+{n2}) = {fmt(S.root_sign)}   "
              f"eps({n1})eps({n2}) = {fmt(E.root_sign * F.root_sign)}   "
              f"deg {S.deg} = {E.deg}+{F.deg}   "
              f"m+ {S.central_order} = {E.central_order}+{F.central_order}")
    print()
    print("  Twist invariance,  (Q, a) -> (cQ, ca):")
    for c in [2.0 + 0j, -1.0 + 0j, 0.3 + 1.1j]:
        Bt = twist(B, c)
        Bt.check_axioms()
        At = twist(A, c)
        At.check_axioms()
        print(f"    c = {fmt(c):>18s}   eps(A^c) = {fmt(At.root_sign)}   "
              f"eps(B^c) = {fmt(Bt.root_sign)}")


def demo_odd_degree(Q: complex) -> None:
    banner("5.  ODD DEGREE FORCES CENTRAL VANISHING")
    # d = 3: one +Q fixed point plus one duality pair; no -Q fixed point.
    E = DualEigensystem(
        Q=Q, alpha=(Q, 2.3 + 1.1j, Q ** 2 / (2.3 + 1.1j)), sigma=(0, 2, 1)
    )
    E.check_axioms()
    print(f"    degree d              = {E.deg}  (odd)")
    print(f"    a -Q fixed point?     = {'yes' if E.nu else 'no'}")
    print(f"    a fixed point exists? = "
          f"{'yes' if any(E.sigma[i] == i for i in range(E.deg)) else 'no'}")
    print(f"    central multiplicity  = {E.central_order}  (odd)")
    print(f"    root sign eps         = {fmt(E.root_sign)}  = (-1)^d")
    print(f"    P(1/Q)                = {fmt(E.char_poly(1 / E.Q))}")
    print()
    print("  An involution of an odd-sized set must have a fixed point; with no")
    print("  -Q fixed point allowed, that fixed point carries +Q, so m+ is odd,")
    print("  eps = -1, and the characteristic polynomial vanishes at the centre.")


def demo_analytic_bridge(systems: Sequence[Tuple[str, DualEigensystem]]) -> None:
    banner("6.  ANALYTIC BRIDGE   Lambda(2-s) = eps Lambda(s),  "
           "(-1)^ord = eps = (-1)^{m+}")
    print(f"{'system':26s} {'max FE error':>14s} {'ord_{s=1}':>10s} "
          f"{'(-1)^ord':>9s} {'eps':>6s}")
    print("-" * 78)
    for name, E in systems:
        if not E.is_involutive:
            continue
        L = cmath.log(E.Q)
        worst = 0.0
        for s in [0.4 + 0.3j, 1.9 - 0.7j, 2.6 + 1.2j, 1.0 + 0j]:
            lhs = E.completed_L(2 - s, L)
            rhs = E.root_sign * E.completed_L(s, L)
            worst = max(worst, abs(lhs - rhs) / max(1.0, abs(rhs)))
        r = numerical_order_of_vanishing(lambda s: E.completed_L(s, L), 1.0 + 0j)
        print(f"{name:26s} {worst:14.3e} {r:10d} {(-1) ** r:+9d} "
              f"{E.root_sign_from_central_order():+6d}")
    print()
    print("  The order of vanishing is measured numerically, by Cauchy integrals")
    print("  for the Taylor coefficients of the entire function Lambda around")
    print("  s = 1.  Its parity always reproduces the combinatorial sign, and in")
    print("  every case here it equals m+ on the nose.")


def demo_sharpness(Q: complex) -> None:
    banner("7.  SHARPNESS: EVERY HYPOTHESIS IS LOAD-BEARING")

    print("  (a)  A single -Q fixed point flips the sign (degree 1):")
    for name, E in [("alpha = +Q", pos_fixed(Q)), ("alpha = -Q", neg_fixed_one(Q))]:
        print(f"       {name:12s} prod alpha = {fmt(E.prod_alpha):>14s}   "
              f"Q^d = {fmt(Q ** E.deg):>14s}   eps = {fmt(E.root_sign)}   "
              f"(-1)^d = {(-1) ** E.deg:+d}")
    print()

    print("  (b)  Two -Q fixed points cancel: hypothesis FAILS, conclusion HOLDS.")
    E = two_neg_fixed(Q)
    print(f"       nu = {E.nu} (even)   prod alpha = {fmt(E.prod_alpha)}   "
          f"Q^2 = {fmt(Q ** 2)}   eps = {fmt(E.root_sign)}")
    print()

    print("  (c)  Two-cycles are sign-neutral, whatever the eigenvalue:")
    for a in [1.0 + 0j, 5.5 - 3.2j, 0.04 + 0.01j]:
        E = duality_pair(Q, a)
        print(f"       a = {fmt(a):>20s}   prod alpha = {fmt(E.prod_alpha):>14s}"
              f"   eps = {fmt(E.root_sign)}")
    print()

    print("  (d)  Degree 4: the sign is not a function of the degree alone.")
    for name, E in [("two pairs", two_pairs(Q, 1.3 + 0.4j, -2.2 + 0.7j)),
                    ("(+Q, -Q, a, Q^2/a)", mixed_deg4(Q, 1.9 - 0.5j))]:
        print(f"       {name:20s} prod alpha = {fmt(E.prod_alpha):>16s}   "
              f"eps = {fmt(E.root_sign)}   (-1)^d = {(-1) ** E.deg:+d}")
    print()

    print("  (e)  Involutivity cannot be weakened to bijectivity.")
    E = three_cycle(Q)
    E.check_axioms(require_involutive=False)
    print(f"       sigma = 3-cycle; fixed points: "
          f"{[i for i in range(3) if E.sigma[i] == i]} (none!)")
    print(f"       duality holds at every index, but sigma o sigma != id.")
    print(f"       prod alpha = {fmt(E.prod_alpha)}   "
          f"-Q^3 = {fmt(-Q ** 3)}   Q^3 = {fmt(Q ** 3)}")
    print(f"       eps = {fmt(E.root_sign)}, i.e. (-1)^(d+1), not (-1)^d.")
    print()
    print("       Reason: chasing a_i a_{sigma(i)} = Q^2 around a 3-cycle forces")
    print("       a_0 = a_2 and then a_0^2 = Q^2, so the cycle is constant +-Q.")


def demo_random_stress_test(n_trials: int = 400, seed: int = 20260823) -> None:
    banner("8.  RANDOMISED STRESS TEST OF THE THREE SIGN FORMULAS")
    import random

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    failures = 0
    for _ in range(n_trials):
        Q = complex(rng.uniform(0.4, 3.0), rng.uniform(-2.0, 2.0))
        if abs(Q) < 0.3:
            continue
        n_pairs = rng.randint(0, 3)
        n_pos = rng.randint(0, 3)
        n_neg = rng.randint(0, 3)
        alpha: List[complex] = []
        sigma: List[int] = []
        for _ in range(n_pairs):
            a = complex(rng.uniform(-3, 3), rng.uniform(-3, 3))
            if abs(a) < 0.2:
                a = 0.5 + 0.5j
            k = len(alpha)
            alpha += [a, Q ** 2 / a]
            sigma += [k + 1, k]
        for _ in range(n_pos):
            k = len(alpha)
            alpha.append(Q)
            sigma.append(k)
        for _ in range(n_neg):
            k = len(alpha)
            alpha.append(-Q)
            sigma.append(k)
        if not alpha:
            continue
        E = DualEigensystem(Q=Q, alpha=tuple(alpha), sigma=tuple(sigma))
        E.check_axioms()
        eps = E.root_sign
        s1 = E.root_sign_from_fixed_points()
        s2 = E.root_sign_from_central_order()
        T = complex(rng.uniform(0.3, 2.0), rng.uniform(0.3, 2.0))
        lhs = (Q ** 2 * T) ** E.deg * E.char_poly(1 / (Q ** 2 * T))
        rhs = eps * Q ** E.deg * E.char_poly(T)
        ok = (close(eps, s1) and close(eps, s2)
              and abs(lhs - rhs) <= 1e-5 * max(1.0, abs(rhs)))
        if not ok:
            failures += 1
            print(f"    FAILURE: Q={Q}, alpha={alpha}, sigma={sigma}")
    print(f"    {n_trials} random duality eigensystems tested "
          f"(degrees 1-12, random complex Q).")
    print(f"    Formulas checked:  eps (definition)  ==  (-1)^(d+nu)  "
          f"==  (-1)^{{m+}},")
    print(f"    plus the functional equation at a random point.")
    print(f"    Failures: {failures}")


def main() -> None:
    Q: complex = 1.6 + 0.7j  # nothing requires Q real or positive

    systems: List[Tuple[str, DualEigensystem]] = [
        ("d=1, +Q fixed point", pos_fixed(Q)),
        ("d=1, -Q fixed point", neg_fixed_one(Q)),
        ("d=2, duality pair", duality_pair(Q, 1.7 - 0.9j)),
        ("d=2, two -Q fixed", two_neg_fixed(Q)),
        ("d=4, two pairs", two_pairs(Q, 1.3 + 0.4j, -2.2 + 0.7j)),
        ("d=4, (+Q,-Q,a,Q^2/a)", mixed_deg4(Q, 1.9 - 0.5j)),
        ("d=3, 3-cycle (NOT inv.)", three_cycle(Q)),
    ]

    print(__doc__.split("Run:")[0].rstrip())
    print(f"\nHalf-weight used throughout:  Q = {fmt(Q)}")

    demo_sign_law(systems)
    demo_functional_equation(systems)
    demo_central_parity(systems)
    demo_structure(Q)
    demo_odd_degree(Q)
    demo_analytic_bridge(systems)
    demo_sharpness(Q)
    demo_random_stress_test()

    banner("SUMMARY")
    print("""
    prod a_i    = (-1)^nu Q^d                       (duality sign law)
    eps         = (-1)^(d + nu) = (-1)^{m+}          (central parity law)
    P(T)        = (1 - QT)^{m+} G(T),  G(1/Q) != 0   (exact central order)
    eps = -1    ==>  P(1/Q) = 0                      (central vanishing)
    Lambda(2-s) = eps Lambda(s),  (-1)^ord = eps     (analytic bridge)

    All the sign information in a duality-symmetric spectrum is concentrated
    in the two real points +-Q of the Weil circle -- and there, only in a
    parity.
    """)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

demos.name: Exhaustive Enumeration of Duality Involutions in Small Degree
demos.description: An exhaustive combinatorial verification. For each degree d from 1 to 6 the program enumerates every involution of the index set (1, 2, 4, 10, 26, 76 of them — the telephone numbers), and for each involution every admissible eigenvalue assignment: each fixed point independently carries +Q or -Q, and each two-cycle carries a generic reciprocal pair. All 705 resulting duality eigensystems are checked against the sign law, both formulas for the sign, the functional equation at a random point, central vanishing whenever the sign is -1, and the sharp converse 'product equals Q^d if and only if the number of anti-diagonal fixed points is even'. Because the sign depends only on the degree and the fixed-point data, degree 6 already exhausts every combinatorial pattern an involution can present.
demos.code:
"""Exhaustive Enumeration of Duality Involutions in Small Degree.

For every degree d from 1 to 6 this enumerates *all* involutions sigma of
{0, ..., d-1}, and for each of them every admissible eigenvalue assignment
drawn from a fixed alphabet (each fixed point independently +Q or -Q, each
two-cycle a generic pair {a, Q^2/a} with a random a).  For every one of the
resulting duality eigensystems it verifies, exactly:

    (1)  prod a_i          == (-1)^nu * Q^d                (sign law)
    (2)  eps               == (-1)^(d + nu) == (-1)^{m_+}   (central parity)
    (3)  the functional equation at a random test point
    (4)  P(1/Q) == 0  whenever eps == -1                    (central vanishing)
    (5)  eps == +1 whenever the eigenvalue product is exactly Q^d and d even,
         i.e. the sharp converse "product = Q^d  iff  nu even"

The enumeration is complete for d <= 6: since the sign depends only on the
degree and the fixed-point data, this exhausts every combinatorial pattern an
involution can present in those degrees.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import random
from typing import Iterator, List, Sequence, Tuple

TOL: float = 1e-7


def involutions(n: int) -> Iterator[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    """Yield every involution of {0, ..., n-1} as a tuple sigma."""
    if n == 0:
        yield ()
        return
    elements = list(range(n))

    def rec(remaining: List[int], sigma: List[int]) -> Iterator[Tuple[int, ...]]:
        if not remaining:
            yield tuple(sigma)
            return
        i = remaining[0]
        rest = remaining[1:]
        sigma[i] = i                                    # i is a fixed point
        yield from rec(rest, sigma)
        for j in rest:                                  # i pairs with j
            sigma[i], sigma[j] = j, i
            yield from rec([r for r in rest if r != j], sigma)
            sigma[i], sigma[j] = i, j
        sigma[i] = i

    yield from rec(elements, [0] * n)


def assignments(sigma: Sequence[int], Q: complex,
                rng: random.Random) -> Iterator[Tuple[complex, ...]]:
    """Yield every eigenvalue family compatible with the involution sigma."""
    n = len(sigma)
    fixed = [i for i in range(n) if sigma[i] == i]
    cycles = sorted({(min(i, sigma[i]), max(i, sigma[i]))
                     for i in range(n) if sigma[i] != i})
    for signs in itertools.product([1, -1], repeat=len(fixed)):
        alpha: List[complex] = [0j] * n
        for i, s in zip(fixed, signs):
            alpha[i] = s * Q
        for (i, j) in cycles:
            a = complex(rng.uniform(-3, 3), rng.uniform(-3, 3))
            if abs(a) < 0.3:
                a = 0.7 + 0.9j
            alpha[i], alpha[j] = a, Q ** 2 / a
        yield tuple(alpha)


def char_poly(alpha: Sequence[complex], T: complex) -> complex:
    p: complex = 1.0 + 0j
    for a in alpha:
        p *= 1 - a * T
    return p


def check(alpha: Sequence[complex], sigma: Sequence[int], Q: complex,
          rng: random.Random) -> bool:
    d = len(alpha)
    nu = sum(1 for i in range(d)
             if sigma[i] == i and abs(alpha[i] + Q) < TOL)
    m_plus = sum(1 for a in alpha if abs(a - Q) < TOL)
    prod: complex = 1.0 + 0j
    for a in alpha:
        prod *= a
    scale = max(1.0, abs(Q) ** d)

    if abs(prod - (-1) ** nu * Q ** d) > 1e-6 * scale:
        return False
    eps = (-1.0) ** d * prod / Q ** d
    if abs(eps - (-1) ** ((d + nu) % 2)) > 1e-6:
        return False
    if abs(eps - (-1) ** (m_plus % 2)) > 1e-6:
        return False
    T = complex(rng.uniform(0.4, 2.0), rng.uniform(0.4, 2.0))
    lhs = (Q ** 2 * T) ** d * char_poly(alpha, 1 / (Q ** 2 * T))
    rhs = eps * Q ** d * char_poly(alpha, T)
    if abs(lhs - rhs) > 1e-5 * max(1.0, abs(rhs)):
        return False
    if eps.real < 0 and abs(char_poly(alpha, 1 / Q)) > 1e-8:
        return False
    if (abs(prod - Q ** d) < 1e-6 * scale) != (nu % 2 == 0):
        return False
    return True


def main() -> None:
    rng = random.Random(11235)
    Q = 1.7 - 0.6j
    grand_total = 0
    print(f"half-weight Q = {Q}\n")
    print(f"{'d':>2s} {'involutions':>12s} {'eigensystems':>13s} {'failures':>9s}")
    print("-" * 42)
    for d in range(1, 7):
        n_inv = 0
        n_sys = 0
        failures = 0
        for sigma in involutions(d):
            n_inv += 1
            for alpha in assignments(sigma, Q, rng):
                n_sys += 1
                if not check(alpha, sigma, Q, rng):
                    failures += 1
                    print("   FAILURE:", sigma, alpha)
        grand_total += n_sys
        print(f"{d:2d} {n_inv:12d} {n_sys:13d} {failures:9d}")
    print("-" * 42)
    print(f"total duality eigensystems verified: {grand_total}")
    print("\nEvery one satisfies the sign law, both sign formulas, the functional")
    print("equation, central vanishing when the sign is -1, and the sharp converse.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

algorithms.name: Central-Parity Root Sign Computation
algorithms.description: The fastest possible determination of the functional-equation sign. By the Central Parity Law the sign equals (-1) raised to the multiplicity m+ of the central eigenvalue +Q in the spectrum, so the entire duality permutation — which is auxiliary data and generally expensive to reconstruct — is irrelevant. The algorithm is a single pass over the eigenvalue list counting matches with the half-weight, giving time complexity O(d) and space complexity O(1) beyond the input, with d the degree (the Betti number). The same count is simultaneously the exact order of vanishing of the characteristic polynomial at the central point T = 1/Q, because the polynomial factorises as (1 - QT)^{m+} G(T) with G(1/Q) nonzero; hence the routine also certifies central vanishing whenever it returns -1. Numerically the only delicacy is the tolerance used to decide equality with Q, which should be scaled relative to |Q|.
algorithms.pseudocode:
INPUT:  half-weight Q (nonzero), eigenvalue list alpha[0..d-1], tolerance tol
OUTPUT: root sign eps in {+1, -1}, central multiplicity m_plus,
        flag central_vanishing

1.  if |Q| <= tol then ERROR 'half-weight must be nonzero'
2.  m_plus <- 0
3.  for i <- 0 to d-1 do
4.        if |alpha[i] - Q| <= tol * max(1, |Q|) then
5.              m_plus <- m_plus + 1
6.  end for
7.  if m_plus mod 2 = 1 then eps <- -1 else eps <- +1
8.  central_vanishing <- (m_plus > 0)
                        // guaranteed true whenever eps = -1
9.  return (eps, d, m_plus, central_vanishing)

CORRECTNESS: eps = (-1)^(d + nu) by the sign law, and d + nu = m_plus mod 2
             because the non-fixed indices, and the non-fixed indices carrying
             the central eigenvalue, both come in duality pairs.
COMPLEXITY:  O(d) arithmetic operations, O(1) extra space.
algorithms.code:
"""Central-Parity Root Sign Computation.

Computes the functional-equation sign of a duality eigensystem in O(d) time
using only the multiset of eigenvalues -- the duality permutation is not
needed, by the Central Parity Law  eps = (-1)^{m_+}.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Sequence, Tuple

TOL: float = 1e-9


def central_multiplicity(alpha: Sequence[complex], Q: complex,
                         tol: float = TOL) -> int:
    """m_+ = number of eigenvalues equal to the central value +Q.

    This is also the exact order of vanishing of P(T) = prod (1 - a_i T)
    at the central point T = 1/Q, by the central factorisation
    P(T) = (1 - QT)^{m_+} G(T) with G(1/Q) != 0.
    """
    return sum(1 for a in alpha if abs(a - Q) <= tol * max(1.0, abs(Q)))


def root_sign(alpha: Sequence[complex], Q: complex, tol: float = TOL) -> int:
    """The functional-equation sign eps = (-1)^{m_+} in {+1, -1}."""
    if abs(Q) <= tol:
        raise ValueError("the half-weight Q must be nonzero")
    return -1 if central_multiplicity(alpha, Q, tol) % 2 else 1


def root_sign_with_certificate(
    alpha: Sequence[complex], Q: complex, tol: float = TOL
) -> Tuple[int, int, int, bool]:
    """Return (eps, degree, m_+, central_vanishing).

    ``central_vanishing`` records whether P(1/Q) = 0, which the theory
    guarantees whenever eps = -1 (m_+ odd, hence positive).
    """
    d = len(alpha)
    m_plus = central_multiplicity(alpha, Q, tol)
    eps = -1 if m_plus % 2 else 1
    return eps, d, m_plus, m_plus > 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    Q = 1.6 + 0.7j
    a = 1.9 - 0.5j
    spectra = {
        "degree 1, +Q":          [Q],
        "degree 1, -Q":          [-Q],
        "degree 2, duality pair": [a, Q ** 2 / a],
        "degree 2, two -Q":      [-Q, -Q],
        "degree 4, mixed":       [Q, -Q, a, Q ** 2 / a],
    }
    for name, spec in spectra.items():
        eps, d, m, van = root_sign_with_certificate(spec, Q)
        print(f"{name:24s} d={d}  m+={m}  eps={eps:+d}  "
              f"P(1/Q)=0? {'yes' if van else 'no'}")

algorithms.name: Duality Pairing Reconstruction and Fixed-Point Census
algorithms.description: Recovers the duality involution from the raw spectrum and audits the whole structure. Each eigenvalue a is matched greedily with its reflection Q^2/a: if a equals its own reflection it is declared a fixed point (necessarily +Q or -Q), otherwise it is paired with an unused eigenvalue equal to Q^2/a. Failure to find a partner is a proof that the multiset is not stable under the reflection and hence not a duality spectrum at all. The routine then reports the full census — number of two-cycles, number of +Q and -Q fixed points, central multiplicity, eigenvalue product against its predicted value — and cross-checks the two independent formulas for the sign, (-1)^(d+nu) from the reconstructed permutation and (-1)^{m+} from the spectrum alone. Their agreement is a nontrivial consistency test that detects, among other things, a duality permutation that is bijective but not involutive. The naive matching loop is O(d^2); replacing the inner scan by a hash table keyed on rounded complex values reduces this to expected O(d), at the cost of the usual floating-point bucketing care.
algorithms.pseudocode:
INPUT:  half-weight Q, eigenvalue list alpha[0..d-1], tolerance tol
OUTPUT: involution sigma (or FAIL), full fixed-point census, both signs

PHASE 1 — reconstruct the involution
1.  used[0..d-1] <- false;  sigma[0..d-1] <- undefined
2.  for i <- 0 to d-1 do
3.        if used[i] then continue
4.        target <- Q^2 / alpha[i]
5.        if |alpha[i] - target| <= tol then
6.              sigma[i] <- i;  used[i] <- true      // self-dual
7.        else
8.              find j != i with used[j] = false and |alpha[j] - target| <= tol
9.              if no such j then return FAIL        // not a duality spectrum
10.             sigma[i] <- j;  sigma[j] <- i;  used[i] <- used[j] <- true
11. end for

PHASE 2 — census
12. F     <- { i : sigma[i] = i }
13. nu    <- |{ i in F : |alpha[i] + Q| <= tol }|
14. m_plus<- |{ i       : |alpha[i] - Q| <= tol }|
15. cycles<- (d - |F|) / 2
16. prod  <- product of all alpha[i]

PHASE 3 — cross-check the two sign formulas
17. eps_sigma   <- (-1)^((d + nu) mod 2)
18. eps_central <- (-1)^(m_plus mod 2)
19. consistent  <- (eps_sigma = eps_central)
20. return (sigma, cycles, |F| - nu, nu, m_plus, prod, (-1)^nu * Q^d,
            eps_sigma, eps_central, consistent)

COMPLEXITY: O(d^2) as written; O(d) expected with a hash table on rounded keys.
algorithms.code:
"""Duality Pairing Verification and Fixed-Point Census.

Given a half-weight Q and a multiset of eigenvalues, this reconstructs a
duality involution sigma with a_i * a_{sigma(i)} = Q^2 by greedy matching of
each eigenvalue with its reflection Q^2/a, and reports the full fixed-point
census (nu, m_+, number of free two-cycles).  It also verifies that the two
independent formulas for the sign,

        eps = (-1)^{d + nu}      and      eps = (-1)^{m_+},

agree -- a nontrivial consistency check on the duality structure.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

TOL: float = 1e-9


def build_duality_involution(
    alpha: Sequence[complex], Q: complex, tol: float = 1e-7
) -> Optional[List[int]]:
    """Greedily construct an involution sigma with a_i a_{sigma(i)} = Q^2.

    Returns ``None`` if the multiset is not stable under the reflection
    a -> Q^2/a, in which case it is not a duality spectrum at all.
    """
    d = len(alpha)
    sigma: List[int] = [-1] * d
    used: List[bool] = [False] * d
    for i in range(d):
        if used[i]:
            continue
        target = Q ** 2 / alpha[i]
        if abs(alpha[i] - target) <= tol * max(1.0, abs(Q)):
            sigma[i] = i          # self-dual: a fixed point of the reflection
            used[i] = True
            continue
        partner = None
        for j in range(d):
            if j != i and not used[j] and \
                    abs(alpha[j] - target) <= tol * max(1.0, abs(Q)):
                partner = j
                break
        if partner is None:
            return None
        sigma[i], sigma[partner] = partner, i
        used[i] = used[partner] = True
    return sigma


def census(alpha: Sequence[complex], Q: complex,
           tol: float = 1e-7) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Full fixed-point census plus the two sign computations."""
    d = len(alpha)
    sigma = build_duality_involution(alpha, Q, tol)
    if sigma is None:
        return {"valid": False}
    fixed = [i for i in range(d) if sigma[i] == i]
    pos_fixed = [i for i in fixed if abs(alpha[i] - Q) <= tol * max(1.0, abs(Q))]
    neg_fixed = [i for i in fixed if abs(alpha[i] + Q) <= tol * max(1.0, abs(Q))]
    m_plus = sum(1 for a in alpha if abs(a - Q) <= tol * max(1.0, abs(Q)))
    nu = len(neg_fixed)
    eps_sigma = (-1) ** ((d + nu) % 2)
    eps_central = (-1) ** (m_plus % 2)
    prod = 1.0 + 0j
    for a in alpha:
        prod *= a
    return {
        "valid": True,
        "degree": d,
        "sigma": sigma,
        "two_cycles": (d - len(fixed)) // 2,
        "pos_fixed": len(pos_fixed),
        "neg_fixed": nu,
        "central_multiplicity": m_plus,
        "prod_alpha": prod,
        "predicted_prod": (-1) ** nu * Q ** d,
        "eps_from_sigma": eps_sigma,
        "eps_from_central_order": eps_central,
        "consistent": eps_sigma == eps_central,
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    Q = 2.0 + 0.0j
    a = 3.0 + 1.0j
    spectrum = [Q, -Q, a, Q ** 2 / a, -Q]
    report = census(spectrum, Q)
    for key, value in report.items():
        print(f"{key:24s} {value}")

algorithms.name: Analytic Order of Vanishing by Cauchy Coefficient Extraction
algorithms.description: An independent, purely analytic route to the same sign. Writing Q = e^L and substituting T = e^{-sL} turns the duality substitution T -> 1/(Q^2 T) into the reflection s -> 2 - s and places the central point at s = 1; the completed function Lambda(s) = e^{(s-1)dL/2} P(e^{-sL}) is then entire and satisfies Lambda(2-s) = eps Lambda(s). The algorithm measures the order of vanishing of Lambda at s = 1 by extracting Taylor coefficients through the Cauchy integral formula, discretised on a circle of fixed radius by the trapezoidal rule. For analytic integrands this quadrature converges geometrically in the number of nodes, so a few hundred nodes give near machine precision. The least index whose coefficient exceeds a relative threshold is the order r, and the theory predicts (-1)^r = eps = (-1)^{m+}. Cost is O(N * (d + K)) for N quadrature nodes, degree d and K candidate orders; accuracy is governed by the contour radius, which must be smaller than the distance to the nearest other zero of Lambda.
algorithms.pseudocode:
INPUT:  half-weight Q, eigenvalue list alpha[0..d-1],
        contour radius rho, node count N, maximum order K
OUTPUT: order of vanishing r of Lambda at s = 1, and the sign (-1)^r

1.  L <- any complex logarithm of Q
2.  define P(T)      <- product over i of (1 - alpha[i] * T)
3.  define Lambda(s) <- exp((s-1) * d * L / 2) * P(exp(-s * L))
4.  scale <- max over the N contour nodes of |Lambda(node)|
5.  threshold <- max(scale, 1) * 1e-7
6.  for k <- 0 to K do
7.        acc <- 0
8.        for t <- 0 to N-1 do
9.              theta <- 2*pi*t/N
10.             z     <- 1 + rho * exp(i*theta)
11.             acc   <- acc + Lambda(z) * exp(-i*k*theta)
12.       end for
13.       c_k <- acc / (N * rho^k)          // k-th Taylor coefficient at s = 1
14.       if |c_k| > threshold then return (k, (-1)^k)
15. end for
16. return (K+1, undetermined)               // Lambda is locally zero to order > K

COMPLEXITY: O(N*(d + K)) operations; geometric quadrature convergence in N.
algorithms.code:
"""Analytic Order of Vanishing by Cauchy Coefficient Extraction.

The completed function of a duality eigensystem is

        Lambda(s) = exp((s-1) d L / 2) * P(exp(-s L)),      e^L = Q,

which is entire and satisfies Lambda(2-s) = eps * Lambda(s).  This algorithm
measures the order of vanishing r = ord_{s=1} Lambda numerically, by
extracting the Taylor coefficients

        c_k = (1 / 2 pi i) * contour-integral of Lambda(z) / (z-1)^{k+1},

discretised on a circle by the trapezoidal rule (spectrally accurate for
analytic integrands), and returning the least k with |c_k| above a relative
threshold.  The theory predicts (-1)^r = eps = (-1)^{m_+}, so this is an
independent, purely analytic route to the combinatorial sign.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import cmath
import math
from typing import Callable, Sequence, Tuple


def char_poly(alpha: Sequence[complex], T: complex) -> complex:
    """P(T) = prod (1 - a_i T)."""
    p: complex = 1.0 + 0j
    for a in alpha:
        p *= 1 - a * T
    return p


def completed_L(alpha: Sequence[complex], Q: complex, s: complex) -> complex:
    """Lambda(s) = e^{(s-1) d L / 2} P(e^{-sL}) with L = log Q."""
    L = cmath.log(Q)
    d = len(alpha)
    return cmath.exp((s - 1) * d / 2 * L) * char_poly(alpha, cmath.exp(-s * L))


def taylor_coefficient(f: Callable[[complex], complex], center: complex,
                       k: int, radius: float = 0.35,
                       n_nodes: int = 512) -> complex:
    """The k-th Taylor coefficient of an analytic f at ``center``."""
    acc: complex = 0.0 + 0j
    for t in range(n_nodes):
        theta = 2 * math.pi * t / n_nodes
        acc += f(center + radius * cmath.exp(1j * theta)) * \
            cmath.exp(-1j * k * theta)
    return acc / (n_nodes * radius ** k)


def order_of_vanishing(f: Callable[[complex], complex], center: complex,
                       max_order: int = 12, radius: float = 0.35,
                       n_nodes: int = 512) -> int:
    """Least k with a nonvanishing Taylor coefficient of f at ``center``."""
    scale = max(
        abs(f(center + radius * cmath.exp(2j * math.pi * t / n_nodes)))
        for t in range(n_nodes)
    )
    threshold = max(scale, 1.0) * 1e-7
    for k in range(max_order + 1):
        if abs(taylor_coefficient(f, center, k, radius, n_nodes)) > threshold:
            return k
    return max_order + 1


def analytic_sign(alpha: Sequence[complex], Q: complex) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """Return (order of vanishing at s = 1, its sign (-1)^order)."""
    r = order_of_vanishing(lambda s: completed_L(alpha, Q, s), 1.0 + 0j)
    return r, (-1) ** r


if __name__ == "__main__":
    Q = 1.6 + 0.7j
    a = 1.9 - 0.5j
    cases = {
        "d=1, +Q":        [Q],
        "d=1, -Q":        [-Q],
        "d=2, pair":      [a, Q ** 2 / a],
        "d=3, +Q + pair": [Q, a, Q ** 2 / a],
        "d=4, mixed":     [Q, -Q, a, Q ** 2 / a],
    }
    for name, spec in cases.items():
        m_plus = sum(1 for x in spec if abs(x - Q) < 1e-9)
        r, sign = analytic_sign(spec, Q)
        print(f"{name:16s} m+={m_plus}  ord={r}  (-1)^ord={sign:+d}  "
              f"(-1)^m+={(-1) ** m_plus:+d}")

visualizations.name: The Weil Circle: Duality Pairs Cancel, Only the Real Points Carry the Sign
visualizations.description: Four panels on the circle of radius Q in the complex plane, each showing a duality-symmetric spectrum. Blue chords join each eigenvalue to its duality partner Q^2/alpha; the two real points +Q and -Q, the only fixed points of the reflection, are marked distinctly. The panels demonstrate visually that adding or moving chords never changes the sign, that a single +Q fixed point flips it, that a -Q fixed point is invisible to the central multiplicity, and that in a mixed configuration only the parity of m+ survives. Each panel's caption reports the degree, the number of two-cycles, m+, nu and the resulting sign.
visualizations.code:
"""Visualisation: the Weil circle and the duality reflection.

Draws the circle |z| = Q in the complex plane, places a spectrum of Frobenius
eigenvalues on it, and joins each eigenvalue to its duality partner
Q^2/a = conj(a) (for |a| = Q) by a chord.  The two *real* points +-Q are the
fixed points of the reflection -- and, by the sign law, the only places where
the functional-equation sign can be born.  Two-cycles (chords) always cancel;
the multiplicity m_+ of the marked point +Q determines eps = (-1)^{m_+}.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def spectrum_on_circle(Q: float, angles: List[float], n_pos: int,
                       n_neg: int) -> List[complex]:
    """Build a duality-symmetric spectrum on the circle of radius Q."""
    alpha: List[complex] = []
    for th in angles:
        alpha.append(Q * complex(math.cos(th), math.sin(th)))
        alpha.append(Q * complex(math.cos(th), -math.sin(th)))
    alpha += [complex(Q, 0.0)] * n_pos
    alpha += [complex(-Q, 0.0)] * n_neg
    return alpha


def draw(ax, Q: float, angles: List[float], n_pos: int, n_neg: int,
         title: str) -> None:
    circle_t = np.linspace(0.0, 2 * math.pi, 512)
    ax.plot(Q * np.cos(circle_t), Q * np.sin(circle_t),
            color="#94a3b8", lw=1.2, zorder=1)
    ax.axhline(0.0, color="#e2e8f0", lw=0.8, zorder=0)
    ax.axvline(0.0, color="#e2e8f0", lw=0.8, zorder=0)

    for th in angles:
        x, y = Q * math.cos(th), Q * math.sin(th)
        ax.plot([x, x], [y, -y], color="#38bdf8", lw=1.6, alpha=0.85, zorder=2)
        ax.scatter([x, x], [y, -y], s=70, color="#0284c7",
                   edgecolor="white", zorder=3)

    if n_pos:
        ax.scatter([Q], [0.0], s=190, marker="o", color="#dc2626",
                   edgecolor="white", zorder=4)
        ax.annotate(f"+Q  (x{n_pos})", (Q, 0.0), textcoords="offset points",
                    xytext=(10, 12), fontsize=11, color="#dc2626",
                    fontweight="bold")
    if n_neg:
        ax.scatter([-Q], [0.0], s=190, marker="s", color="#7c3aed",
                   edgecolor="white", zorder=4)
        ax.annotate(f"-Q  (x{n_neg})", (-Q, 0.0), textcoords="offset points",
                    xytext=(-8, 14), ha="right", fontsize=11, color="#7c3aed",
                    fontweight="bold")

    d = 2 * len(angles) + n_pos + n_neg
    eps = (-1) ** (n_pos % 2)
    ax.set_title(
        f"{title}\nd = {d},  two-cycles = {len(angles)},  "
        f"m$_+$ = {n_pos},  " + r"$\nu$ = " + f"{n_neg},   "
        + r"$\varepsilon$ = " + f"{eps:+d}",
        fontsize=11)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    lim = 1.45 * Q
    ax.set_xlim(-lim, lim)
    ax.set_ylim(-lim, lim)
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_visible(False)


def main() -> None:
    Q = 1.0
    configs: List[Tuple[List[float], int, int, str]] = [
        ([0.7, 1.9, 2.7], 0, 0, "Only two-cycles: sign-neutral"),
        ([0.7, 1.9], 1, 0, "One $+Q$ fixed point: sign flips"),
        ([0.7, 1.9], 0, 1, "One $-Q$ fixed point: invisible to $m_+$"),
        ([0.7, 1.9], 1, 2, "Mixed: only $m_+$ mod 2 survives"),
    ]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(18, 5))
    for ax, (angles, n_pos, n_neg, title) in zip(axes, configs):
        draw(ax, Q, angles, n_pos, n_neg, title)
    fig.suptitle(
        "The Weil circle: duality pairs cancel, only the real points "
        r"$\pm Q$ can carry the sign",
        fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.93))
    fig.savefig("weil_circle_duality.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote weil_circle_duality.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

visualizations.name: The Completed Function and Its Central Order of Vanishing
visualizations.description: Two coupled panels. On the left, the completed function Lambda(s) is plotted along the real axis for four spectra; the reflection identity Lambda(2-s) = eps Lambda(s) is directly visible as evenness about the dashed central line when the sign is +1 and as oddness — forcing a zero at the centre — when the sign is -1. On the right, the same curves are shown as |Lambda| on a logarithmic scale, where a zero of order m+ appears as a downward spike whose depth grows with the order, making the identity 'sign = parity of the central order of vanishing' visible to the eye.
visualizations.code:
"""Visualisation: the completed function and its order of vanishing.

For a duality eigensystem with half-weight Q > 0 the completed function

        Lambda(s) = e^{(s-1) d L / 2} P(e^{-s L}),      L = log Q,

is entire and satisfies Lambda(2-s) = eps Lambda(s).  Plotting Lambda along
the real axis makes the symmetry about s = 1 visible to the eye: when
eps = +1 the graph is even about the central point, and when eps = -1 it is
odd, forcing Lambda(1) = 0.  The right-hand panel shows |Lambda| on a log
scale, where the order of vanishing appears as the slope of a straight line.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import List, Sequence

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def char_poly(alpha: Sequence[complex], T: complex) -> complex:
    p: complex = 1.0 + 0j
    for a in alpha:
        p *= 1 - a * T
    return p


def completed_L(alpha: Sequence[complex], Q: float, s: complex) -> complex:
    L = math.log(Q)
    d = len(alpha)
    return np.exp((s - 1) * d / 2 * L) * char_poly(alpha, np.exp(-s * L))


def main() -> None:
    Q = 2.0
    a = 1.3 + 1.52j            # |a| is irrelevant to the sign
    a = Q ** 2 / abs(a) ** 2 * a if abs(a) else a
    cases = [
        ("even: two duality pairs", [a, Q ** 2 / a, -a, -Q ** 2 / a]),
        ("odd: one $+Q$, one pair", [complex(Q, 0), a, Q ** 2 / a]),
        ("even: one $-Q$, one pair", [complex(-Q, 0), a, Q ** 2 / a]),
        ("odd: three $+Q$", [complex(Q, 0)] * 3),
    ]

    s_vals = np.linspace(0.05, 1.95, 601)
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5.6))
    colours = ["#0ea5e9", "#dc2626", "#7c3aed", "#f59e0b"]

    for (label, spec), colour in zip(cases, colours):
        vals = np.array([completed_L(spec, Q, complex(s, 0.0)).real
                         for s in s_vals])
        m_plus = sum(1 for x in spec if abs(x - Q) < 1e-9)
        eps = (-1) ** (m_plus % 2)
        ax1.plot(s_vals, vals, color=colour, lw=2,
                 label=f"{label}   " + r"$\varepsilon$" + f" = {eps:+d}")
        ax2.semilogy(s_vals, np.abs(vals) + 1e-18, color=colour, lw=2,
                     label=f"$m_+$ = {m_plus}")

    for ax in (ax1, ax2):
        ax.axvline(1.0, color="#334155", ls="--", lw=1.2)
        ax.set_xlabel("$s$")
        ax.legend(fontsize=9, loc="best")
        ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
    ax1.axhline(0.0, color="#94a3b8", lw=0.9)
    ax1.set_ylabel(r"$\Lambda(s)$")
    ax1.set_title(r"$\Lambda(2-s) = \varepsilon\,\Lambda(s)$:"
                  "\neven about $s=1$ iff " + r"$\varepsilon = +1$")
    ax2.set_ylabel(r"$|\Lambda(s)|$  (log scale)")
    ax2.set_title("Order of vanishing at the centre:\n"
                  r"a zero of order $m_+$ shows as a downward spike")

    fig.suptitle("The sign is the parity of the central order of vanishing",
                 fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.92))
    fig.savefig("lambda_central_vanishing.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote lambda_central_vanishing.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

interactive_demos.description: A hands-on laboratory for the sign law. Click anywhere in the upper half of the circle of radius Q to drop a duality two-cycle — a point together with its mirror partner Q^2/alpha — and use the buttons to add or remove the two self-dual eigenvalues +Q and -Q, the only fixed points of the reflection. A slider varies the half-weight Q. The panel on the right recomputes, live, the degree, the number of two-cycles, the count nu of anti-diagonal fixed points, the central multiplicity m+, the normalised eigenvalue product, and the functional-equation sign obtained in three logically independent ways: from the fixed-point formula (-1)^(d+nu), from the intrinsic central-parity formula (-1)^{m+}, and from a numerical measurement of the order of vanishing of the completed function at the central point. Below it, the completed function Lambda(s) is plotted across the critical strip with the central line marked, so the reflection identity Lambda(2-s) = eps Lambda(s) is visible as evenness or oddness about that line. The decisive experiment is to pile up chords: however many two-cycles are added, and wherever they sit, the sign never moves — all of it is concentrated in the parity of the number of copies of +Q.

interactive_demos.title: The Involutivity Stress Test: Chasing Duality Around a Cycle
interactive_demos.description: An interactive dissection of the one hypothesis that cannot be dropped. The duality permutation is replaced by a k-cycle rather than an involution, and the constraint alpha_i * alpha_{i+1} = Q^2 is propagated arrow by arrow around the cycle from a chosen starting eigenvalue. Sliders control the cycle length k and the angle of alpha_0 on the circle; the closing arrow turns green when the chain is consistent and red-dashed when it is not. Even cycles always close and behave like disguised unions of pairs. Odd cycles close only at the two real points: land on alpha_0 = -Q and the widget exhibits a completely legal duality spectrum with no fixed point whatsoever — so the hypothesis 'no anti-diagonal fixed point' holds vacuously — whose eigenvalue product is minus Q^k instead of Q^k. The verdict panel explains at each configuration exactly which hypothesis has been broken and why the pairing argument fails, making concrete that involutivity, not fixed-point-freeness, is what the proof consumes.
